_note: Season periodization (GDD 4.8). The training year as phases tied to the target meets; every number and text of the season model is here. Weeks are whole Monday-to-Sunday weeks. A phase starts at an anchor ('season_start', the indoor target's week or the outdoor target's week) plus `weeks`; the player can move each start by up to shift_limit weeks, and every phase keeps at least min_phase_weeks. A phase with `omit_without` is left out when the season has no target of that kind (the phase before it then lasts longer; the neighbours still count from the fallback date below). Week plans: days = 7 lists of session ids (Mon..Sun), intensity = 7 x easy / normal / hard. A week is built in this order: the phase's week, ramp, lighter week, easy day before a race, taper (see SeasonPlan.week_for).

season._note: A season starts on the Monday nearest to start_month/start_day (2 Nov 2026, 1 Nov 2027, 30 Oct 2028) and runs until the next one.

anchor_fallback._note: Only used for the phase edges when a season has no target of that kind (no meet fits the athlete). Month and day in the season's second calendar year; an estimate, not a real meet.

phases.name: General base
phases.text: Build the engine: easy running, strength and the club group. Every fourth week is lighter.

phases.name: Indoor specific
phases.text: Sharpen up for the indoor target: 800 m intervals and the first races.

phases.name: Spring base
phases.text: Back to building: tempo runs, hills and strength before the outdoor season. Every fourth week is lighter.

phases.name: Pre-competition
phases.text: Switching to race preparation: speed work and the first outdoor races.

phases.name: Race season
phases.text: Racing season: keep the speed, race often and recover well.

phases.name: Transition
phases.text: A few easy weeks to rest the body and the mind after the summer.

phases.name: Autumn general
phases.text: A gentle start to the new training year before the next general base.

lighter._note: In phases with lighter weeks every `every`-th week of the phase: every day `step_down` intensity steps down (Hard > Normal > Easy). Not in a taper week.

ramp._note: The first ramp_weeks weeks of a phase blend in from the previous phase's week, a day at a time: in ramp week k (0-based) the first round((k+1) x 7 / ramp_weeks) days are the new phase's, the rest the previous phase's. 1 = no ramp.

easy_day_before_race._note: In race phases the day before an entered race (same week, not a race or rest day) is set to this intensity.

taper._note: Counted back from the target's race day (days = days before it). Bands are checked in order; the first that contains the day applies. max_sessions: keep only the best session (keep_tags first: a session with the first tag wins, then the second; ties = the first listed); replace: session swapped for another; sessions: the day becomes exactly these sessions (not on a rest day); intensity: set the day's intensity; rest: a rest day. Wins over lighter weeks and the easy day before a race. {meet} and {days} are filled in.

bands.why: Taper: {meet} in {days} days, one sharp session

coach_pick._note: The coach's star plan (GDD 4.8), from what the player can see: attributes as shown (whole numbers) and injuries (tiers listed; niggles and illnesses don't count). Steady after `injuries` or more injuries in the last `months` months or with durability <= durability_max; Ambitious with durability >= durability_min, professionalism >= professionalism_min and no injury in the last `injury_free_months` months; otherwise Balanced. Youth limits (user, 2026-10-07): with 6 / 12 two in three new 14-year-olds were pointed to Steady and nobody to Ambitious.

offer._note: The club coach's offer of the three plans (GDD 4.8, M2 step 6f): a stop event when a career starts on the coach's star plan, and each autumn `weeks_before` weeks before the next season starts (season mode only). 'Decide later' (or no choice) = the season starts on the coach's star plan of that day. Choosing a plan enters the season's target meets where allowed. {season} = '2027-28', {targets}, {age_class}, {date}, {plan}, {n}, {s} are filled in.
offer.title_first: Your coach has three plans for the season
offer.title_next: Your coach has three plans for next season ({season})
offer.text_first: Your club coach has written the training year in three versions. They differ in how much and how hard you train. The ★ is the coach's pick for you. Your target meets: {targets}; you're entered in them.
offer.text_next: Next season you race as {age_class}. The coach's target meets: {targets}. When you choose a plan, you're entered in them where you can be.
offer.no_targets: none for your age class in the calendar yet
offer.later: Decide later in the Training tab
offer.later_first: You stay on the ★ plan ({plan}). You can change it any time under Training, Change plan.
offer.later_next: If you don't choose before {date}, the season starts on the coach's ★ plan.
offer.star_note: ★ = your coach's pick for you now (from your durability, professionalism and injuries in the last year). Weekly load is the season's average week; the risk word is what most weeks of the plan read.
offer.replace: This replaces your changes to {n} phase{s} of that season with the coach's {plan} plan. Your targets and moved edges stay.
offer.next_open: Choose your plan for next season before {date}. If you don't, the season starts on the coach's ★ plan.
offer.next_chosen: Next season starts on {date} with {plan}. You can still change it here until then.

return_block._note: much_safer: when the plan risk word is the same with and without the block, the event says the block is much safer if its expected injuries are at most this share of the full plan's. Easing back in after a layoff (GDD 4.8 'Return block', M2 step 6f). After at least min_days days in a row without running (any reason), on the evening before the first day with an allowed run in the plan, the club coach offers it (Accept / No thanks), once per layoff. Its weeks are 7-day spans from the first day back; `lengths`: the last entry whose min_days fits the layoff gives the weeks' kinds. Kinds: max_sessions a day (the kept session: a kept hard one, else one tagged run_tag, else the first), sessions with a swap_tag become easy_session except the first `keep_hard` sessions with a keep_tag per week, intensity at most intensity_max; or step_down = every day that many steps easier (a lighter week). Race days are left alone; the day before a race is Easy. It wins over the lighter week, the easy day before a race and the taper. Works in both plan modes.

first.text: One session a day, all Easy, no hard or fast sessions
first.why: Easing back in, week {week} of {weeks}: one easy session

second.text: One session a day at Normal, one hard session kept
second.why: Easing back in, week {week} of {weeks}: one session, one hard one a week

lighter.text: A lighter week of your plan
lighter.why: Easing back in, week {week} of {weeks}: a lighter week

ui.title: Easing back in
ui.text: You haven't run for {days} days{cause}. From tomorrow you may run again. Your coach suggests {weeks} weeks to ease back in:
ui.then_season: Then your season plan ({phase}) as usual.
ui.then_repeat: Then your weekly plan as usual.
ui.risk_full: Straight back to your full plan
ui.risk_note: Your body has lost some of what it was used to while you weren't running, so the same plan as before is a bigger step now.
ui.risk_same_safer: Both read {risk}, but easing back in is much the safer of the two: the full plan is the bigger jump.
ui.risk_same_low: Both read Low: your body is still used to running, so the easier weeks are a gentle extra.
ui.risk_same: Both read {risk}: the weeks after it are still a big step up. Easy days, or the Steady plan for a while, would lower it.
ui.races: Entered in this time: {races}. Your entries stay; the day before a race is easy.
ui.accept_detail: You can stop it early in the Training tab.
ui.decline_detail: Your plan stays as it is.
ui.caption: Easing back in · week {week} of {weeks}
ui.box_text: Your club coach's easy way back after {days} days without running. Your plan comes back bit by bit, then carries on as before.
ui.stop_ask: Stop easing back in? From today your full plan applies again, and its plan risk may be high.

variants._note: The club coach's three season plans (GDD 4.8; tuned in M2 step 6d with tools/training_balance.gd part 4, numbers in GDD 4.8 'Built (step 6d)'). Per variant: name, text, card (the Training tab's plan card: focus, and the typical week's plan risk as measured in 6d: most weeks of the season read this word), ramp_weeks per phase and one week template per phase (days = Mon..Sun session lists, intensity = 7 x easy / normal / hard). Every plan keeps a full rest day each week. Balanced's general base is exactly the coach's starter week (data/training.json), so a new career starts as before. Easy days are the cheap way to train: Easy cuts body strain to 0.6 but keeps 0.8 of the effect (data/health.json).

steady.name: Steady
steady.text: The coach's normal sessions, but most days easy. Low risk, slower progress.

ambitious.name: Ambitious
ambitious.text: A big year: two sessions on most days, built up gradually. Faster progress, but it pays only if you listen to your body.
